Marcus — quick ops note:

We have high confidence this is a dedicated-GPU pool saturation case compounded by a KV-cache eviction storm. Symptoms: concurrent long sequences, sudden spike in peak-sequence length, and a single job (non-QuantBank tenant) started a heavy-attention workload causing continuous high mem usage on the node set. The serving runtime applied kernel fallbacks leading to increased per-token latency and transient 5xx when pool-level queueing exceeded soft limits.

Immediate actions I've initiated:
- Isolated the noisy tenant and throttled their allocations (taking effect now).
- Triggered a rebalancer job to move QuantBank slots off the hot nodes (ETA 10–18m).
- Pushing a short-lived KV-cache bypass for high-cardinality keys to reduce eviction churn.
- Collected ops log snippets and pushed to the thread (ops_log_snippets.txt).

If burst capacity is approved we should see p50 back to normal in ~20m after rebalancer completes; otherwise the hosted traffic-shift Marcus proposed is the safest stopgap.

Irene Choi
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
